narrative_synthesis: The meta shifted from seller-finance tactics to legacy and honesty: family wealth stories, 'not passive income' confessions, and sell-or-hold dilemmas with real numbers. Drafts for today: (1) a short legacy story post, (2) a Philly sell-or-hold dilemma, (3) a 'not passive' reply magnet.

drafts.draft_en:
Generational wealth rarely starts big.

It starts with one boring asset somebody refused to sell.

One rowhouse. One business. One paid-off duplex.

Then the next generation adds one more.

What's the first asset in your family's story?
drafts.pattern: legacy story + 'that's generational wealth' framing + reply question
drafts.video_tip: Talking head in front of a Philly rowhouse. If you have a real family story (first property, first business), tell it in the first 5 seconds instead of the generic lines. 30-45s.

drafts.draft_en:
You own a Philly duplex.

Worth $[value]. Owe $[balance]. Clears $[cash flow] a year.

Option A: sell, 1031 into a bigger building.
Option B: hold forever and let it pay you.

Which are you picking?
drafts.video_tip: Skip video, or a 15s screen of the three numbers with A/B on screen. Fill the brackets with real or clearly hypothetical Philly numbers before posting, and reply to every answer in the first hour.

drafts.draft_en:
Real estate isn't passive income.

It's a business with a slow paycheck.

Tenants, repairs, taxes, vacancy. It all shows up eventually.

What's the one repair that ate a whole year of cash flow on yours?
drafts.video_tip: Quick selfie clip, say line one to camera in the first 2 seconds. Under 20s. Swap in your own worst repair if you have one.
